title: Constant coefficient tensor comparison
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, let $T,U$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Work on small representatives of their small etale sites in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], in the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(S_{\Et},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $Rj_*$ for the unbounded K-injective derived direct image and $j^{-1}\dashv Rj_*$ for the derived adjunction of [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Suppose that $Rj_*$ preserves countable coproducts. For every $K\in D(U_{\Et},A)$ and every finite $A$-module $N$ (finite as a set, equivalently finitely generated since $A$ is finite), the canonical tensor comparison is an isomorphism:
$$
 (Rj_*K)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N_T
 \longrightarrow Rj_*(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N_U).
$$
Here $N_T,N_U$ are the constant module sheaves, placed in degree zero [def-kun-constant-sheaf], the tensors are ordinary uncompleted etale derived tensors [def-kun-derived-tensor], and the displayed morphism is $\mathrm{PF}_j(K,N_T)$ of [def-kun-projection-formula-map] under the canonical identification $j^{-1}N_T\simeq N_U$.

proof.text: Construct the finite-free resolution explicitly, without a finite-projective-dimension assumption. Set $M_0=N$. Given the finite module $M_r$, put $P^{-r}=A^{M_r}$, map its basis vector $e_x$ to $x\in M_r$, and let $M_{r+1}$ be this map's kernel. Since both $A$ and $M_r$ are finite, $P^{-r}$ and $M_{r+1}$ are finite sets. For $r\geq1$ define $d^{-r}:P^{-r}\to P^{-r+1}$ by the surjection onto $M_r$ followed by the kernel inclusion $M_r\hookrightarrow P^{-r+1}$; set $P^i=0$ for $i>0$. Thus $d^2=0$; for $r\geq2$ one has $\operatorname{im}d^{-r}=M_r=\ker d^{-r+1}$, while $\operatorname{im}d^{-1}=M_1$ is the kernel of the augmentation $P^0\to N$. The augmentation is surjective, so $P\to N[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: successive finite free covers of kernels; explicit finite-set construction

proof.text: For $S=T,U$, apply the constant-sheaf construction [def-kun-constant-sheaf] termwise to $P\to N[0]$. The constant presheaf construction is exact sectionwise, and sheafification is exact and commutes with colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact]. Consequently the augmentation $P_S\to N_S[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $(P_S)^{-r}\simeq A_S^{M_r}$. Apply [lem-kun-pullback-constant], whose statement covers modules and complexes of modules, to obtain the canonical isomorphisms $\gamma_N:j^{-1}N_T\xrightarrow{\sim}N_U$ and $\gamma_P:j^{-1}P_T\xrightarrow{\sim}P_U$. Their compatibility with augmentation can be checked explicitly: for any module homomorphism $h:M\to M'$, the adjuncts of $\gamma_{M'}j^{-1}(h_T)$ and $h_U\gamma_M$ under the module adjunction [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] are maps $M_T\to j_*M'_U$ sending every constant section $x$ on an etale $W\to T$ to the constant section $h(x)$ on $W\times_TU$. They are equal by the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Apply this equality to every differential of $P$ and to $P^0\to N$; thus the comparisons form a chain isomorphism and commute with the augmentation.

proof.text: For the fixed $K$, put $F(L)=(Rj_*K)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}L$ and $G(L)=Rj_*(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}j^{-1}L)$ on $D(T_{\Et},A)$, and let $\alpha_L=\mathrm{PF}_j(K,L)$ [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] to the ringed topoi with constant rings $A_T,A_U$. The coefficient pullback is the exact module inverse image by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so its derived functor is $j^{-1}$. The cited mate theorem states that $F,G$ are exact, $\alpha$ is natural and shift-compatible, and $\alpha_{A_T}$ is the identity under tensor-unit identifications. Hence $\alpha$ is invertible on shifts and finite sums of $A_T$: exact functors are additive, and naturality with the finitely many injections and projections identifies the component on a finite biproduct with the biproduct of the components.

source.place: Tags 06YU (definition-derived-tor), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map); unit and shift structures of the cited mate theorem

proof.text: For $m\geq0$ let $E_m$ be the brutal truncation of $P_T$ keeping degrees $-m,\ldots,0$. The inclusions $E_m\to E_{m+1}$ are chain maps. Prove by induction that $\alpha_{E_m}$ is invertible. The base $E_0=(P_T)^0[0]$ is a finite sum of $A_T$. For $m\geq1$ there is a degreewise split short exact sequence of complexes $0\to E_{m-1}\to E_m\to(P_T)^{-m}[m]\to0$, where the last term has its sole nonzero sheaf in degree $-m$. Its triangle is distinguished by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. The mate theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] makes $\alpha$ a morphism between its $F$- and $G$-images, including the connecting square. Its first and third components are invertible by induction and the preceding step, so [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] gives invertibility of the middle component $\alpha_{E_m}$. This proves the induction for all $m$.

source.place: Tags 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), 014A (lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle); finite stupid-truncation argument also sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0944 (lemma-projection-formula), proof

proof.text: For the sequence $E_0\to E_1\to\cdots$, the degreewise colimit is exactly $P_T$: in degree $i\leq0$ the sequence is constantly $(P_T)^i$ with identity transition maps once $m\geq-i$, and all positive degrees are zero. Apply [lem-kun-complex-colimit-hocolim] in sheaves of $A_T$-modules on the small etale site. With $B=\bigoplus_{m\geq0}E_m$ in the derived category and $s\iota_m=\iota_{m+1}(E_m\to E_{m+1})$, it gives the distinguished telescope triangle $B\xrightarrow{1-s}B\to P_T\to B[1]$. In particular it identifies the telescope with this specific complex, by the quasi-isomorphism from the cone to the degreewise colimit; no claim of unique functorial cones is needed.

Both $F$ and $G$ preserve the countable coproduct in the preceding step. For $F$ this is [lem-kun-derived-tensor-direct-sums]. For $G$, first $j^{-1}$ preserves coproducts by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], applied to the derived adjunction $j^{-1}\dashv Rj_*$ specified in [def-kun-projection-formula-map]; then tensoring with $K$ preserves them by [lem-kun-derived-tensor-direct-sums]; finally $Rj_*$ preserves them by the hypothesis of the item. These are coproducts over the small discrete category $\mathbf N$, in the chosen universe; there is no appeal to an arbitrary large index category.

source.place: Tag 0038 (lemma-adjoint-exact), part (1); derived tensor coproduct theorem applied over the countable set N

proof.text: Under the coproduct identifications from the preceding step, naturality gives $\alpha_B F(\iota_m)=G(\iota_m)\alpha_{E_m}$ for every $m$. Therefore $\alpha_B$ is the coproduct of the isomorphisms $\alpha_{E_m}$; its inverse is induced by their inverses, as is checked on each coprojection. Apply the exact functors $F,G$ to the telescope triangle of step 5. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], the components $(\alpha_B,\alpha_B,\alpha_{P_T})$ give a morphism of distinguished triangles. In particular, if $q:P_T\to B[1]$ is the connecting map, its final square is $s_GG(q)\alpha_{P_T}=\alpha_B[1]s_FF(q)$, where $s_F,s_G$ identify the images of $B[1]$ with $F(B)[1],G(B)[1]$. This follows from naturality at $q$ and the cited shift compatibility; it is the actual canonical component at $P_T$, not an arbitrarily chosen telescope comparison. Its first two components are isomorphisms, so [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] proves that $\alpha_{P_T}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 014A (lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle), applied to the telescope triangle of Tag 090Z (definition-derived-colimit); shift-compatible mate as in step 3

proof.text: Let $a:P_T\xrightarrow{\sim}N_T$ be the augmentation isomorphism of step 2. Naturality of the canonical mate [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] gives $\alpha_{N_T}=G(a)\alpha_{P_T}F(a)^{-1}$, hence this component is invertible. Under $j^{-1}N_T\simeq N_U$ from step 2 it is exactly the comparison asserted in the statement. The resolution may have infinitely many negative terms; the argument used only its finite brutal truncations and their countable telescope, so it does not impose finite projective dimension on $N$ or any boundedness on $K$.
